  "text": "On Sunday, Imani found a small feather caught between the bench slats. It was gray except for a white tip, and it came free when she pulled gently.

The boy arrived with his notebook under his arm. He sat beside her and opened it to the drawing of her hand. The shadow he had added made one finger look longer than the others.

“I found this,” she said, holding up the feather.

He turned to a clean page. Imani set the feather across it, but a breeze lifted the tip. She held it down with one finger while he drew.

A pigeon walked beneath the bench, stopping now and then to peck at the ground. Imani watched its head bob forward. There was a white mark on its wing, but she could not tell whether the feather had belonged to it.

When the boy finished, she let go. The feather slid along the page and settled against the notebook’s fold.

“My grandfather has a jar for things he finds,” she said. “Buttons and keys that don’t open anything.”

“Does he keep feathers?”

“I don’t know.”

They took it to the bakery to ask him. He looked at the feather, then found an empty paper bag. He folded the top twice so it would not blow out on the walk home.

Outside, the pigeon had moved to the far end of the bench. Imani carried the bag in both hands. She could feel almost no weight in it, though she knew the feather was still there."
